chunks: And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who shaved his head before offering his sacrifice; he said, 'There is no harm, and there is nothing upon him, and he should not repeat it.'

And whoever brought along a sacrificial animal with him during the Ten [days of Dhul-Hijjah], if he had let its hair grow and tied a garland around its neck, he should not slaughter it except in Mina on the Day of Sacrifice; and if he had not let its hair grow nor tied a garland around its neck, he should slaughter it in Mecca when he arrives during the Ten [days]; he narrated that.

key_terms.أَشْعَرَهُ: let its hair grow (prerequisite for hady)
key_terms.قَلَّدَهُ: tied a garland around its neck (prerequisite for hady)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhul-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim slaughter their sacrificial animal during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that shaving the head prior to the actual sacrifice is permissible and carries no penalty, emphasizing the flexibility in the sequence of Hajj rites. The narration further details the specific locations for slaughtering the *hady*: if the animal was prepared by allowing its hair to grow and tying a garland, it must be slaughtered in Mina on the Day of Sacrifice; otherwise, it may be slaughtered in Mecca upon the pilgrim's arrival. This distinction highlights the scholarly emphasis on the ritual state of the animal in determining the validity and location of the offering.
